external_source.relevant_observation: Headroom mixes lossless and lossy/recoverable transforms; CCR recovery is side-store/marker based and source comments document a nested-marker recovery hazard. This E4 therefore tests only a side-store-free pure lossless structural transform, not Headroom import or CCR.

experiment.candidate: self-describing row-oriented structural encoding with fixed field contract and source ContextView digest; no omitted fields, no semantic summarization, no external recovery store
experiment.token_measurement_limit: NO_PINNED_TARGET_TOKENIZER_AVAILABLE; lexical-token and chars/4 proxies only
experiment.unrelated_environment_note: Python subprocess startup emitted an artifact-tool spreadsheet warmup timeout, but the experiment process completed and its JSON stdout parsed successfully. Classified as infrastructure noise, not an F2 scientific negative.

observations: The fixed structural header is net-negative for a one-item view and must not be blindly enabled for tiny contexts.
From four selected items upward the synthetic F2-style structure shows positive byte reduction; the gain plateaus near 36% by 256 selected items.
Exact canonical round-trip identity held for every benchmark size.
All six malformed/tampered representations were rejected fail-closed.

Measured encode/decode overhead remained sub-millisecond through 64 selected items in this environment and approximately 2.5 ms each at 256 items; these are local research timings, not target-runtime measurements.

architecture_delta.placement: derived noncanonical transient stage after ContextView selection and before any model-facing serialization that otherwise repeats full metadata keys
architecture_delta.activation_hypothesis: enable only when measured rendered-token savings exceed codec/header overhead; tiny contexts should bypass
architecture_delta.missing_gate: measure actual F2 production model-facing renderer output on representative admitted ContextViews with the exact pinned target tokenizer, then run downstream task/lesion equivalence and latency accounting
